title: Pre-Start Meeting Minutes
author: Priya Nandakumar (Halvern Build Ltd)

pages.text:
Aldermoor Court – Pre-Start Meeting
Minutes of meeting held on Wednesday 3 September 2025, 10:00, Halvern Build site office, 14 Aldermoor Road, Eastbrook.

Present: Sasha Morel (Eastbrook Living Housing Association, Client Representative); Priya Nandakumar (Halvern Build Ltd, Project Manager); Dana Whitlock (Halvern Build Ltd, Site Manager); Ewa Lindqvist (Halvern Build Ltd, H&S Advisor); Lena Okafor (Okafor Lind Architects); Jonas Brightwell (Brightmere Structural); Hugo Calder (Calder & Voss Engineering). Apologies: Rui Tanaka (Eastbrook Building Control).

1. Project overview

1.1 Aldermoor Court is a six-storey residential building providing 48 apartments (18 one-bed, 24 two-bed, 6 three-bed) above a single-level basement car park with 62 parking spaces, a plant room, a bin store and a cycle store for 96 bicycles. The basement and its 900 mm reinforced concrete raft sit partly below the groundwater level recorded in the site investigation.

1.2 The works are let under a design and build contract. Halvern Build Ltd took possession of the site on Monday 1 September 2025. The contractual date for practical completion is Wednesday 30 June 2027, giving a contract period of 95 weeks.

1.3 The superstructure is an in-situ reinforced concrete frame with 250 mm flat slabs, enclosed by steel framing system (SFS) infill walls and a brick slip rainscreen. Windows and balcony doors are thermally broken aluminium units.

2. Programme

2.1 PN presented the tender programme. Key early dates: site set-up and hoarding complete by 12 September 2025; bulk excavation and dewatering from 22 September 2025; raft foundation pours planned for January 2026 in three bays.

2.2 SM asked for a monthly programme update to be issued with each progress meeting report. Agreed.

4. Health and safety

4.1 EL presented the construction phase plan. All operatives must attend site induction before starting work. Hard hats, safety boots, high-visibility vests, gloves and eye protection are mandatory beyond the welfare area.

4.2 Excavation below 1.2 m is to be battered or supported; the dewatering system must be checked at the start of every shift and recorded in the site diary.

5. Site rules and working hours

5.1 Permitted working hours are Monday to Friday 07:30 to 18:00 and Saturday 08:00 to 13:00. No noisy work on Sundays or public holidays. Concrete pours that may overrun must be notified to the neighbours on Aldermoor Road at least 48 hours in advance.

5.2 Deliveries are to be booked through the site office at least 24 hours ahead. The loading bay is on Aldermoor Road; vehicles must not wait on the public highway before 07:30.

title: Structural Concrete Specification (Rev C)
author: Jonas Brightwell (Brightmere Structural)

pages.text:
ALD-SPEC-0310 Rev C – Structural Concrete Specification
Aldermoor Court, 14 Aldermoor Road, Eastbrook. Issued for construction.

1 General

1.1 Scope. This specification covers the supply, placing, compaction, curing and testing of all in-situ structural concrete for Aldermoor Court, including blinding, the basement raft foundation, basement retaining walls, columns, core walls, ground floor slab, suspended flat slabs at Levels 1 to 5 and the roof slab.

1.2 Standards. Concrete shall be specified, produced and conformity-assessed in accordance with EN 206 and its national complementary standard. Execution shall comply with EN 13670 to Execution Class 2. Design is to EN 1992-1-1 and EN 1992-3 with the National Annex. Reinforcement shall be grade B500B to EN 10080.

1.3 Submissions. The Contractor shall submit the proposed mix design for every concrete type to the Engineer at least 4 weeks before the first pour of that concrete type. Each submission shall state the strength class, exposure classes, cement type, total binder content, water-cement ratio, admixtures and dosages, maximum aggregate size, consistence class and chloride class.

1.4 Revisions. Rev C supersedes Rev B dated 21 July 2025. Changes: clause 2.3 (basement walls) amended to add exposure class XA2 following the sulfate results in the supplementary ground investigation; clause 4.2 (crystalline admixture) added; clause 5.6 (cold weather) clarified.

1.5 Definitions. Water-cement ratio means the ratio of free water to total cementitious content (cement plus any ground granulated blast-furnace slag or fly ash counted in accordance with EN 206). Binder content means the total cementitious content in kg/m³.

2 Concrete schedule

2.1 Blinding: strength class C12/15, minimum thickness 75 mm, laid within 24 hours of formation approval.

2.2 Raft foundation (900 mm thick): strength class C32/40; exposure classes XC2 and XA2; maximum water-cement ratio 0.45; minimum binder content 340 kg/m³; cement CEM III/A 42.5N; crystalline waterproofing admixture to clause 4.2; consistence class S3; maximum aggregate size 20 mm; nominal cover 75 mm to bottom face and 50 mm to top face.

2.3 Basement retaining walls (350 mm thick): strength class C32/40, exposure classes XC4, XD3 and XA2, maximum water-cement ratio 0.45, minimum binder content 340 kg/m³. Cement shall be CEM III/A 42.5N, or CEM I with not less than 50% ground granulated blast-furnace slag. A crystalline waterproofing admixture shall be included to clause 4.2. Consistence class S4; maximum aggregate size 20 mm; chloride class Cl 0,40. Nominal cover 50 mm to the external (earth) face and 45 mm to the internal (car park) face.

2.4 Columns (300 x 600 mm): strength class C40/50, exposure class XC1, nominal cover 30 mm. Columns in the car park shall additionally be protected by the impact barriers shown on the architectural drawings.

2.5 Core and shear walls: strength class C32/40, exposure class XC1, nominal cover 30 mm.

2.6 Ground floor slab (300 mm) and suspended flat slabs at Levels 1 to 5 (250 mm): strength class C32/40, exposure class XC1, consistence class S3, nominal cover 25 mm top and bottom. The soffit of the ground floor slab over the car park shall have 35 mm cover for fire resistance R120.

2.7 Roof slab (275 mm): strength class C32/40, exposure class XC3, nominal cover 35 mm top and 25 mm bottom.

2.8 The car park running surface (top of raft) shall be power floated to class SR2 and receive the deck coating system specified by the Architect.

3 Basement waterproofing

3.1 Design approach. The basement shall be protected using combined protection. Type B (structurally integral) protection is provided by the raft and retaining walls with the crystalline admixture. In addition, Type C (drained cavity) protection is required to the plant room and cycle store, which shall achieve a Grade 3 environment. The car park shall achieve a Grade 2 environment: no water penetration acceptable, some moisture vapour tolerable.

3.2 Construction joints. All kicker joints and vertical construction joints in the raft and basement walls shall incorporate a hydrophilic waterbar strip together with a re-injectable injection hose. Hose ends shall be brought out to accessible junction boxes, labelled and recorded on the joint record drawing. Kickers shall be cast monolithically with the raft and be not less than 150 mm high.

3.3 Crack control. Basement walls and raft are designed for a maximum crack width of 0.2 mm. Any crack wider than 0.2 mm, or any crack showing moisture, shall be reported to the Engineer and repaired by resin injection to a method statement approved by the Engineer.

3.4 Penetrations. Service penetrations through the raft or basement walls shall be formed only with cast-in puddle-flange sleeves to the Engineer's detail. Core drilling of basement walls is not permitted without written approval.

4 Admixtures

4.1 General. Admixtures shall comply with EN 934-2. Admixtures containing chlorides are not permitted. The combination of admixtures in any mix shall be confirmed as compatible by the supplier.

4.2 Crystalline waterproofing admixture. The raft and basement wall concrete shall contain a crystalline waterproofing admixture, AquaLock CX or equal approved, dosed at 1.0% by mass of total binder unless otherwise agreed by the Engineer. The admixture shall be added at the batching plant, not on site. Its use does not relax any requirement of this specification for water-cement ratio, binder content, cover or crack width.

5 Execution

5.1 Pre-pour inspection. The Contractor shall give the Engineer at least 48 hours' notice of every pour of the raft, basement walls, transfer elements and suspended slabs. No concrete shall be placed until the Engineer has inspected the reinforcement, cover, cast-in items and formwork and has given approval to pour.

5.2 Placing. Concrete shall be placed within 2 hours of batching. The free fall of concrete shall not exceed 1.5 m; tremie or pump hose shall be used in wall forms. Walls shall be placed in layers not exceeding 500 mm and compacted with internal vibrators.

5.3 Water addition. No water shall be added to concrete on site. Superplasticiser may be added on site only by the supplier's technician, with the dosage recorded on the delivery ticket.

5.4 Curing. Concrete shall be protected from drying immediately after placing. Elements in exposure class XD3 or XA2 shall be cured for a minimum of 7 days; all other elements for a minimum of 4 days. Wall formwork shall remain in place for at least 3 days, after which curing shall continue using an approved curing membrane or wet hessian under polythene.

5.5 Striking. Slab soffit formwork shall not be struck until test cubes cured alongside the slab have reached 25 N/mm² and not earlier than 7 days after casting. Back-propping shall be maintained through the two floors below the slab being cast.

5.6 Cold weather. Concrete shall not be placed when the air temperature is below 3°C and falling, or on frozen ground or reinforcement. The concrete temperature at delivery shall be at least 5°C. Freshly placed concrete shall be protected with insulated blankets when frost is forecast within 72 hours of placing.

5.7 Hot weather. The concrete temperature at delivery shall not exceed 30°C.

6 Testing and acceptance

6.1 Sampling. One set of three 100 mm cubes shall be taken for every 50 m³ of each concrete type, with a minimum of one set per pour or per day. One cube of each set shall be tested at 7 days and two at 28 days. Additional cubes shall be cast and site-cured for striking decisions on suspended slabs.

6.2 Consistence. A slump or flow test shall be carried out on the first delivery of each pour and thereafter on every fifth truck, and on any truck that appears visibly different.

6.3 Records. The Contractor shall keep a pour record for each pour stating the element, grid location, volume, start and finish times, air temperature, delivery ticket numbers, test results and the names of the supervising foreman and inspector.

6.4 Non-conformity. Where 28-day results do not meet the characteristic strength, the Contractor shall inform the Engineer within 24 hours and propose investigation, which may include cores to EN 12504-1.

7 Tolerances and finishes

7.1 Slab level: ±10 mm from the specified level. Slab flatness: 5 mm under a 2 m straightedge for areas receiving screed-free finishes.

7.2 Wall verticality: 10 mm over the storey height. Position of cast-in channels and sleeves: ±10 mm.

7.3 Basement walls shall have a Class B fair-faced finish to the car park face. Tie holes shall be plugged with a proprietary waterproof plug system approved by the Engineer.

title: Facade Specification – Brick Slip Rainscreen (Rev B)
author: Lena Okafor (Okafor Lind Architects)

pages.text:
ALD-SPEC-0420 Rev B – Facade Specification: Brick Slip Rainscreen
Aldermoor Court, 14 Aldermoor Road, Eastbrook.

1 General

1.1 Scope. This specification covers the design development, supply and installation of the external wall system to all elevations from Level 1 to the roof parapet, comprising steel framing system (SFS) infill walls, external insulation, ventilated cavity, aluminium support rails and brick slip carrier panels. The ground floor plinth is covered in section 8.

1.2 Responsibility. The facade subcontractor shall complete the detailed design of brackets, rails, fixings and cavity barriers, supported by structural calculations, and is responsible for coordination with the window installation.

1.3 Performance requirements. The completed wall shall achieve:
(a) an area-weighted U-value not exceeding 0.18 W/m²K, calculated to EN ISO 6946;
(b) air permeability of the building envelope not exceeding 3.0 m³/(h·m²) at 50 Pa;
(c) resistance to wind load to EN 1991-1-4 for the site;
(d) a reaction to fire classification of A1 or A2-s1,d0 to EN 13501-1 for all insulation, membranes, brackets, rails and cladding components, except for the small components listed in section 3.

1.4 Revisions. Rev B supersedes Rev A. Insulation thickness increased from 140 mm to 160 mm; mock-up requirements in section 4 expanded.

3 Fire safety

3.1 Cavity barriers shall be installed in the ventilated cavity at every floor level, at the junction with every compartment wall and around every window and door opening. Barriers in the ventilated cavity shall be open-state intumescent cavity barriers providing 60 minutes integrity and 30 minutes insulation, Linebar OS-60 or equal approved.

3.2 The slab edge between the SFS and the slab shall be fire-stopped with a 120-minute linear joint seal, tested to EN 1366-4 for the gap size installed.

3.3 Permitted small components that need not achieve A2-s1,d0 are limited to: window gaskets and seals, EPDM membranes at window reveals not exceeding 300 mm in width, sealants and intumescent materials.

3.4 Installation of cavity barriers shall be photographed and recorded floor by floor, and each floor shall be inspected by the Contractor before the cladding panels close the cavity. Building control shall be offered a sample inspection at Level 1 and at one upper level.

4 Visual and performance mock-up

4.1 Before any brick slip panels are manufactured, the facade subcontractor shall build an on-site mock-up of the external wall, 3.0 m wide by 3.0 m high, including one complete window from the window package, a sill, a window head with cavity barrier, an external corner, a vertical movement joint and brick slip pointing.

4.2 The mock-up must be approved in writing by both the Architect and the Client Representative before brick slip panel production is released. Approval shall cover brick slip colour, mortar colour, joint profile, sill and head details and the visual alignment of rails.

4.3 The approved mock-up shall be retained on site as the quality benchmark until practical completion.

5 Tolerances and workmanship

5.1 Rail alignment: ±2 mm over 2 m and ±5 mm over a storey height. Brick slip joint width: 10 mm ±2 mm. Brick slip panel face flatness: 3 mm under a 1 m straightedge.

5.2 Fixings into concrete shall be installed and proof-tested in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions. A minimum of 3% of post-installed anchors on each floor shall be proof-tested to 1.5 times the design working load.

6 Submittals

6.1 The facade subcontractor shall submit shop drawings and structural calculations for brackets and rails at least 6 weeks before installation begins on site.

6.2 Samples: three brick slip panels showing the colour range; mortar samples; bracket and rail samples; cavity barrier product data with test evidence.

6.3 Test certificates for reaction to fire classification of every component shall be provided before installation.

7 Lead times and sequencing

7.1 Brick slip panels: 8 weeks from written approval of the mock-up. Aluminium brackets and rails: 4 weeks from approved shop drawings. Insulation: 2 weeks.

7.2 Brackets, insulation and rails may be installed before the brick slip panels arrive, provided each floor is weather-protected and the cavity barriers are inspected before closing.

8 Ground floor plinth

8.1 The ground floor plinth shall be 215 mm facing brick, colour Eastbrook Buff Dark, built as masonry cladding on stainless steel wall ties to the SFS, with a full-fill 100 mm mineral wool cavity.

title: Windows and Balcony Doors Specification (Rev B)
author: Lena Okafor (Okafor Lind Architects)

pages.text:
ALD-SPEC-0450 Rev B – Windows and Balcony Doors
Aldermoor Court, 14 Aldermoor Road, Eastbrook.

1 General

1.1 Scope. Supply and installation of 196 aluminium windows and 48 balcony doors to the apartments (244 units in total), including sub-sills, pressed aluminium sills, internal and external membranes, sealants and ironmongery. Communal entrance doors are excluded and specified separately.

1.2 System. Thermally broken aluminium window system Velto AX70 by Velto Windows, or equal approved. Any alternative system shall demonstrate equal or better thermal, acoustic and weather performance by test evidence.

1.3 Product standard. Windows and doors shall be CE/UKCA marked to EN 14351-1.

1.4 Thermal performance. The whole-window thermal transmittance shall not exceed Uw 1.2 W/m²K, calculated to EN ISO 10077 for the standard window size. Glazing shall be double glazed with a centre-pane Ug not exceeding 1.0 W/m²K, warm edge spacers and argon fill.

1.5 Solar control. The total solar energy transmittance (g-value) of the glazing shall not exceed 0.40 on the south and west elevations and 0.50 on the north and east elevations, to limit summer overheating in the apartments.

1.6 Weather performance. Air permeability Class 4 to EN 12207; watertightness Class E750 to EN 12208; resistance to wind load Class C4 to EN 12210.

1.7 Acoustic performance. Generally, the sound reduction of the window in the closed position shall be not less than Rw+Ctr 31 dB. Elevations identified in the acoustic report as requiring higher performance shall be confirmed with the Architect.

2 Materials and finishes

2.1 Frames. Extruded aluminium alloy EN AW-6060 T66 with polyamide thermal breaks.

2.2 Finish. Frames, sashes, sills and external flashings shall be polyester powder coated to Qualicoat Class 2, minimum 60 microns. Colour: RAL 7016 Anthracite Grey, satin (30% gloss), to both internal and external faces.

2.3 Glazing. Safety glazing to EN 12600 Class 1B1 is required in all panes wholly or partly within 800 mm of finished floor level and in all balcony door panes. Toughened glass shall be heat-soak tested.

2.4 Ironmongery. Tilt-and-turn hardware with concealed hinges. All opening lights above ground floor shall be fitted with child-safe opening restrictors limiting the opening to 100 mm, overridable for cleaning and escape.

2.5 Trickle ventilators are not required, as each apartment is provided with whole-house mechanical ventilation with heat recovery (MVHR).

2.6 Sills. External sills shall be 3 mm pressed aluminium, 225 mm deep, with end caps and a minimum 25 mm drip projection beyond the face of the brick slip cladding, finished to match the frames.

3 Installation

3.1 Windows shall be fixed into the SFS openings with stainless steel brackets at maximum 600 mm centres. The installation sequence shall follow the facade subcontractor's sequence so that cavity barriers around the opening are installed and inspected before the window is fixed.

3.2 An internal vapour-tight EPDM membrane and an external vapour-open EPDM membrane shall be bonded to the frame and to the SFS sheathing, providing an airtight and weathertight seal on all four sides.

3.3 Installation tolerance: ±2 mm in the diagonal and level, and the frame shall be centred in the opening with a perimeter gap of 10 to 15 mm.

4 Samples, mock-up and approvals

4.1 One complete window, including sill and membranes, shall be supplied for inclusion in the facade mock-up described in ALD-SPEC-0420 section 4.

4.2 Colour samples of the powder coat finish on aluminium, minimum 150 x 100 mm, shall be submitted for approval with the shop drawings.

4.3 Shop drawings for every window type, together with thermal calculations demonstrating compliance with clause 1.4, shall be submitted to the Architect for approval before manufacture.

5 Lead times

5.1 The supplier has confirmed a manufacturing lead time of 10 weeks from approval of shop drawings and colour, and delivery in floor-by-floor batches to suit the installation sequence.

6 Testing and handover

6.1 Site water tests to the AAMA 501.2 hose test method, or equivalent agreed with the Architect, shall be carried out on 5% of installed windows, selected by the Architect, including at least one window per elevation per floor.

6.2 Handover documentation shall include product declarations of performance, the as-installed schedule of window types by apartment, glass certificates and maintenance instructions.

title: MEP Specification – Basement and Common Systems (Rev A)
author: Hugo Calder (Calder & Voss Engineering)

pages.text:
ALD-SPEC-0510 Rev A – Mechanical, Electrical and Public Health Services: Basement and Common Systems
Aldermoor Court, 14 Aldermoor Road, Eastbrook.

1 General

1.1 Scope. This specification covers the central heating and hot water plant, car park ventilation, electric vehicle (EV) charging, below-ground and car park drainage, sprinkler protection and the coordination of service penetrations through the basement structure. Apartment services (heat interface units, MVHR, small power and lighting) are specified in ALD-SPEC-0520.

1.2 Design criteria. External design temperatures: winter -4°C, summer 28°C dry bulb. Apartment internal design temperature 21°C living rooms, 18°C bedrooms. All plant shall be selected for operation with refrigerants having a global warming potential below 750.

1.3 Coordination. The MEP subcontractor shall produce coordinated installation drawings in 3D, clash-checked against the structural model, before any sleeve, cast-in item or containment is installed.

2 Heating and hot water

2.1 Heat source. Heating and domestic hot water are generated centrally by three 70 kW air source heat pumps operating in cascade, located in the roof plant enclosure, with a 2,000 litre buffer vessel. Flow temperature 55°C; design return temperature 30°C.

2.2 Distribution. Insulated flow and return risers in the two cores serve a heat interface unit (HIU) in each apartment. Each HIU provides instantaneous domestic hot water and heating with individual heat metering.

2.3 Emitters. Apartments are heated by low-temperature radiators sized for a mean water temperature of 45°C.

2.4 Ventilation of apartments. Each apartment has an MVHR unit with a heat recovery efficiency of at least 85% and a specific fan power not exceeding 0.85 W/(l/s).

2.5 Controls. The plant shall be monitored by a building management system with remote access for the facilities manager. Alarms shall be sent by email and SMS.

3 Car park ventilation

3.1 The basement car park shall be ventilated by an impulse (jet fan) system comprising 6 reversible jet fans and 2 main extract fans of 50% duty each, discharging at roof level via a dedicated shaft in core B. Make-up air enters through the ramp opening.

3.2 Normal ventilation is controlled by carbon monoxide (CO) and nitrogen dioxide (NO2) detection. Fans run at low speed when CO exceeds 30 ppm and at high speed when CO exceeds 90 ppm or NO2 exceeds 3 ppm. Smoke clearance mode provides 10 air changes per hour on activation of the fire alarm.

3.3 Extract fans shall be rated F300 (300°C for 60 minutes) to EN 12101-3.

4 EV charging

4.1 Six car parking spaces shall be provided with active 7.4 kW Mode 3 chargers (Type 2 sockets), with load management to limit the total EV demand to the available supply capacity.

4.2 All remaining spaces shall have passive provision: cable containment and spare capacity in the EV distribution board DB-EV1 to allow future chargers to be added without builder's work.

4.3 DB-EV1 shall be fed by a 100 A TP&N sub-main from the main LV panel in the basement plant room.

5 Drainage

5.1 The car park floor drains via slot drains to a Class 1 full-retention separator (petrol interceptor) to EN 858, and then to a pumped sump with duty/standby submersible pumps discharging to the foul sewer. The sump shall have a high-level alarm connected to the BMS.

5.2 The Type C cavity drainage systems in the plant room and cycle store drain to a separate sump with duty/standby pumps and a battery-backed high-level alarm.

6 Sprinkler protection

6.1 The car park shall be protected by a wet-pipe sprinkler system to EN 12845, Ordinary Hazard Group 2. The apartments shall be protected by a residential sprinkler system. Both systems are served from a sprinkler tank and pump set in the basement plant room.

7 Service penetrations through the basement structure

7.1 All services entering the building below ground level shall pass through cast-in puddle-flange sleeves, located and detailed in coordination with the Structural Engineer. Sleeve positions shall be issued on a dedicated sleeve schedule at least 3 weeks before the relevant wall pour.

7.2 No service shall be routed through the raft. Rising mains from the pumped sumps shall exit through the basement walls above the car park slab level.

title: Site Diary – 18 November 2025
author: Dana Whitlock (Halvern Build Ltd)

pages.text:
Site Diary – Aldermoor Court
Tuesday 18 November 2025. Recorded by Dana Whitlock, Site Manager.

Weather: heavy rain overnight and until 11:00 (14 mm recorded on the site gauge), then overcast and dry. Temperature 6°C at 07:30, 9°C at 14:00. Wind south-westerly, 20 to 30 km/h.

Labour on site: Halvern Build 5 (site manager, assistant site manager, engineer, 2 general operatives); Doran Groundworks 13 (excavator drivers, banksmen, dumper drivers, pipe layers). Total 18.

Plant: 2 x 21 t tracked excavators, 1 x 9 t forward-tipping dumper, 6 tonne roller, 2 x 100 mm submersible dewatering pumps plus 1 standby pump.

Works progress: Bulk excavation continued in zones 3 and 4 (north half of the basement footprint, gridlines A to D). Formation level reached in zone 3 at 4.6 m below existing ground level. Groundwater was encountered at approximately 4.2 m below ground level on the north side, consistent with the site investigation. Seepage into the excavation was controlled by the sump pumps at the north-east and north-west corners; water discharged through the settlement tank to the sewer under the temporary discharge consent.

Muck away: 46 loads (approximately 460 m³) removed to the licensed tip. Wheel wash in operation all day; road sweeper attended at 12:00 and 16:30 following rain.

Inspections: Dewatering system checked at 07:30 and 13:00, all pumps running, no fines observed in the discharge. Excavation batters inspected by DW before the start of work and after the rain; minor slumping of the batter at grid A/2 was cut back and covered with polythene sheeting.

Visitors: Jonas Brightwell (Brightmere Structural) inspected the formation in zone 3 at 14:30 and approved it for blinding, subject to removing a soft spot of approximately 2 m² at grid B/3 and replacing it with Type 1 granular fill.

Issues: Rain delayed the start of excavation by approximately 3 hours. Bulk excavation remains forecast to finish by 12 December 2025.

title: Site Diary – 22 January 2026 (Raft Bay 2 Pour)
author: Dana Whitlock (Halvern Build Ltd)

pages.text:
Site Diary – Aldermoor Court
Thursday 22 January 2026. Recorded by Dana Whitlock, Site Manager.

Weather: clear and cold. Temperature 2°C at 06:30 rising to 7°C at 13:00, falling to 3°C by 17:30. Light frost at first light; no precipitation. Forecast overnight minimum -1°C.

Labour on site: Halvern Build 7; concrete gang (Mateus Ferreira, foreman, plus 9 operatives); Brandt Rebar 4 (standby for the pour); Doran Groundworks 6; pump operators 2; Greystone Ready-Mix technician 1. Total 29.

Main activity: Raft foundation Bay 2 (gridlines C to E, 900 mm thick) poured today. Approval to pour was given by Jonas Brightwell at 16:00 on 20 January after the pre-pour inspection, with all hydrophilic strips and injection hoses at the Bay 1 / Bay 2 joint checked and recorded.

Pour record: first truck on site 06:30, pour started 06:50, last truck discharged 17:40. Volume placed 368 m³ in 46 truck loads of mix GRM-3240-XA2-WP (C32/40 with AquaLock CX crystalline admixture). Two 36 m boom pumps used. Concrete temperature at delivery 9 to 12°C. Slump tests on first truck and every fifth truck, all within class S3. Eight sets of cubes taken.

Delays: Truck 31 was rejected at 13:15 because the delivery ticket showed the wrong mix (C32/40 without admixture). Greystone replaced it within 35 minutes. No cold joint formed.

Curing and protection: The top surface was power floated in sections from 15:00 and covered progressively with polythene and two layers of insulated blankets as frost is forecast. Curing to continue for a minimum of 7 days per ALD-SPEC-0310 clause 5.4. Temperature probes installed at the centre and top of the pour; readings to be taken twice daily by the concrete gang.

Other works: Doran Groundworks continued excavation of the ramp at the east side. Brandt Rebar delivered 22 t of reinforcement for Bay 3, stored on bearers in the laydown area.

Deliveries: 46 concrete trucks (Greystone); 22 t reinforcement (Brandt Rebar); 40 insulated blankets (hire).

Health and safety: Pour briefing held at 06:15 by Mateus Ferreira. Exclusion zone maintained around the pumps. Neighbours on Aldermoor Road were notified on 19 January of the extended working hours. No incidents.

Next steps: Raft Bay 3 (gridlines E to H) reinforcement to start on Monday 26 January; pour targeted for Thursday 5 February 2026.

title: Site Diary – 14 March 2026 (Wall W3 Pour Postponed)
author: Dana Whitlock (Halvern Build Ltd)

pages.text:
Site Diary – Aldermoor Court

title: RFI 017 – Basement Wall Concrete: Water-Cement Ratio and Admixture
author: Mateus Ferreira (Halvern Build Ltd)

pages.text:
Request for Information ALD-RFI-017
Subject: Basement wall concrete – water-cement ratio and crystalline admixture
Raised by: Mateus Ferreira, Concrete Foreman (Halvern Build Ltd), 11 February 2026
Addressed to: Jonas Brightwell (Brightmere Structural)
Copy: Dana Whitlock, Priya Nandakumar (Halvern Build); Carys Doyle (Greystone Ready-Mix)
Priority: Urgent – first basement wall pour (W1) planned for 3 March 2026

Background: ALD-SPEC-0310 Rev C clause 2.3 requires the basement retaining walls to be C32/40 with a maximum water-cement ratio of 0.45 and a minimum binder content of 340 kg/m³, with a crystalline waterproofing admixture to clause 4.2. Greystone Ready-Mix has submitted mix GRM-3240-XD3-WP (data sheet ALD-DS-GRM-3240) with a free water-cement ratio of 0.42 and 360 kg/m³ of CEM III/A, with AquaLock CX at 1.0% by mass of binder.

Questions:
(a) Please confirm that the maximum water-cement ratio of 0.45 is calculated on the total cementitious content, including the slag in the CEM III/A.
(b) Greystone has suggested that, because the crystalline admixture reduces permeability, the water-cement ratio could be relaxed to 0.50 to improve pumpability in the 350 mm walls. Is this acceptable?
(c) May superplasticiser be added on site to restore consistence if a truck arrives stiff?

Response from Jonas Brightwell (Brightmere Structural), 16 February 2026:

(a) Confirmed. The water-cement ratio in clause 2.3 is the ratio of free water to total cementitious content, as defined in clause 1.5. The slag in CEM III/A counts in full.

(b) Not accepted. The maximum water-cement ratio of 0.45 is governed by the XD3 and XA2 exposure classes and is not relaxed by the use of the crystalline admixture (see clause 4.2). The submitted mix GRM-3240-XD3-WP, at a water-cement ratio of 0.42, is accepted for the basement walls. Pumpability should be achieved with the superplasticiser dosage at the plant, targeting consistence class S4.

(c) Superplasticiser may be added on site only by Greystone's technician, once per truck at most, with the dose recorded on the delivery ticket, in accordance with clause 5.3. No water shall be added on site under any circumstances.

Additional note: Please ensure the 7-day minimum curing period in clause 5.4 is applied to all basement walls; wall formwork is to stay in place for at least 3 days.

Status: Closed, 16 February 2026.

Background: ALD-SPEC-0420 clause 2.3 requires facade brackets to be fixed to the slab edges with a minimum edge distance of 100 mm. title: Product Data Sheet – AquaLock CX Crystalline Waterproofing Admixture
author: Technical Department (Dorrance Construction Chemicals)

pages.text:
AquaLock CX – Crystalline Waterproofing Admixture for Concrete
Dorrance Construction Chemicals. Product data sheet, edition 10/2025.

Description: AquaLock CX is a dry powder admixture that reacts with water and the by-products of cement hydration to form insoluble crystals within the capillary pores and micro-cracks of concrete. The crystals block the passage of water under hydrostatic pressure while allowing the concrete to breathe.

Uses: basements and below-ground structures, water-retaining structures, car park decks, tunnels, and foundations in aggressive ground. Suitable for structurally integral (Type B) waterproofing systems.

Conformity: EN 934-2, Table 9 (water-resisting admixture). Chloride-free.

Dosage: 0.8% to 1.2% by mass of total binder; 1.0% is recommended for most applications. The admixture shall be added at the batching plant, either in dissolvable bags with the aggregates or as a slurry. Not to be added on site.

Self-sealing: in the presence of moisture, the crystalline reaction can seal static, non-moving cracks up to 0.4 mm wide. Moving cracks and joints must be detailed with waterbars or injection systems. The admixture does not replace the need for correct joint detailing.

Effects on fresh concrete: setting time may be extended by 1 to 2 hours, depending on temperature and cement type. There is no significant effect on workability at the recommended dosage. Compatible with CEM I, CEM II and CEM III cements and with polycarboxylate superplasticisers.

Performance: reduction in water penetration depth under pressure (EN 12390-8) typically 50% or more compared with a control mix of the same constituents.

Curing: normal curing is required. Moist curing for at least 7 days improves the development of the crystalline structure.

Packaging and storage: 6 kg dissolvable bags, 36 kg cartons. Store in dry conditions, off the ground, at 5°C to 35°C. Shelf life 12 months in unopened packaging.

Health and safety: the powder is alkaline. Wear gloves, eye protection and a dust mask when handling. Refer to the safety data sheet.

Technical support: Dorrance Construction Chemicals, technical helpline 0161 555 0230, technical@dorrance-chemicals.example.

author: Jonas Brightwell (Brightmere Structural)

pages.text:
Inspection Report ALD-INS-SE-011 – Basement Watertightness Inspection
Aldermoor Court. Inspected Thursday 9 July 2026, 10:00 to 12:30, by Jonas Brightwell (Brightmere Structural), accompanied by Dana Whitlock and Mateus Ferreira (Halvern Build Ltd).

Conditions: inspection carried out after 31 mm of rain on 7 and 8 July 2026. Groundwater in the monitoring standpipe on the north side was 3.9 m below ground level, approximately 0.7 m above the underside of the raft.

Scope: all internal faces of the basement retaining walls W1 to W8, construction joints, kicker joints, the visible areas of the raft, and all cast-in sleeves S-01 to S-14. The Type C cavity drain membranes in the plant room and cycle store are not yet installed.

Finding 1 (action required): Damp patch approximately 0.6 m long at the vertical construction joint between walls W2 and W3 on the north wall (grid A/3), between 0.9 m and 1.5 m above the car park slab. The surface is wet to the touch but not dripping. This is not acceptable for a Grade 2 environment. Remedy: inject the joint through the pre-installed injection hose W3-H1 with polyurethane resin, followed by acrylic resin, by an approved specialist.

Finding 2 (monitor): Hairline vertical crack in wall W6 (east), grid H/4, measured 0.15 mm wide, dry. Within the 0.2 mm crack width limit. The crystalline admixture is expected to seal static cracks of this size if moisture reaches them. Monitor at each inspection.

Finding 3 (action required): Damp staining around sleeve S-14 (LV duct) in wall W7, plant room. The hydrophilic collar appears not to be fully bonded to the sleeve. Remedy: resin injection around the sleeve from the internal face, and sealing of the annulus with a link seal as required by ALD-RFI-021.

Finding 4 (observation): Kicker joints along walls W1, W4, W5 and W8 were dry. The car park slab had standing rainwater from the ramp opening only, not from the structure.

Conclusion: The basement is broadly performing as designed. Subject to the remedial injection of the W2/W3 joint and sleeve S-14, the car park will achieve the Grade 2 environment required by ALD-SPEC-0310 clause 3.1. A re-inspection is required after the remedial work and the next significant rainfall.

Close-out record (added 30 July 2026): Remedial injection of the W2/W3 joint and sleeve S-14 was carried out by Sealtech Injection Services on Wednesday 15 July 2026. Re-inspected on 29 July 2026 after 18 mm of rain on 27 and 28 July: both locations dry. Findings 1 and 3 closed. Finding 2 remains open for monitoring; the crack in W6 was unchanged and dry.

Signed: Jonas Brightwell, Associate Director, Brightmere Structural.

title: RFI 008 – MVHR Duct Routing Through First Floor Joists
author: Callum Reyes (Halvern Build Ltd)

pages.text:
Request for Information KES-RFI-008
Subject: MVHR duct routing through first floor engineered joists
Raised by: Callum Reyes, Site Manager (Halvern Build Ltd), 21 July 2026
Addressed to: Brackenwood Timber Systems (timber frame designer); Calder & Voss Engineering
Plots affected: all, worst case plots 3 and 6 (handed layouts)

Background: The MVHR layout drawing KES-M-5201 shows 150 mm rigid ducts running across the first floor joist zone from the plant cupboard to the living room and kitchen extract. The engineered I-joists are 245 mm deep. The joist manufacturer's tables allow holes up to 150 mm diameter only in the central zone of the web and not within 300 mm of the supports.

Questions:
(a) Can 150 mm ducts pass through the joist webs at the positions shown?
(b) If not, please advise an alternative route.

Response from Brackenwood Timber Systems and Calder & Voss Engineering, 24 July 2026:

(a) No. At the positions shown the holes would fall within 300 mm of the supports at the stair trimmer. Holes through the webs are permitted only in the central zone and must not exceed 150 mm in diameter, which leaves no tolerance for the duct insulation.

(b) Use 204 x 60 mm flat rectangular ducts through the joist webs, with factory-formed openings in the mid-span zone, as shown on revised drawing KES-M-5201 Rev C. Flow rates are unchanged; the MVHR unit fan setting is to be adjusted at commissioning to compensate for the higher duct resistance.

Status: Closed, 24 July 2026.

title: Airtightness Test Report – Plots 1 to 8
author: Theo Marsh (Airtest North)

pages.text:
Airtightness Test Report KES-INS-004
Kestrel Lane Townhouses, Plots 1 to 8. Tested by Theo Marsh (Airtest North) on Thursday 24 September 2026; re-test of Plot 6 on Thursday 1 October 2026. Report issued 2 October 2026.

Method: building pressurisation test to EN ISO 9972, Method 3 (building envelope with intentional openings sealed), with test results expressed as air permeability at 50 Pa. MVHR terminals, extractor hood duct and soil vent pipe were temporarily sealed.

Design target: air permeability not exceeding 3.0 m³/(h·m²) at 50 Pa, as used in the energy calculations.

Results (24 September 2026):
Plot 1: 2.38. Pass.
Plot 2: 2.55. Pass.
Plot 3: 2.41. Pass.
Plot 4: 2.62. Pass.
Plot 5: 2.47. Pass.
Plot 6: 3.62. Fail.
Plot 7: 2.29. Pass.
Plot 8: 2.70. Pass.

Plot 6 investigation: Smoke testing during depressurisation identified leakage at the junction of the first floor zone with the external wall (around three joist ends where the airtightness membrane was cut for the MVHR flat ducts), around the soil vent pipe where it passes through the vapour control layer in the loft, and at an unsealed electrical back box on the party wall.

Remedial work by Halvern Build on 28 and 29 September 2026: joist end penetrations sealed with airtightness tape and grommets; the soil vent pipe collar replaced; back box fitted with an airtight cover.

Re-test of Plot 6 (1 October 2026): 2.71 m³/(h·m²) at 50 Pa. Pass.

Conclusion: All eight plots now meet the design air permeability of 3.0 m³/(h·m²) at 50 Pa. The results have been passed to the energy assessor for the as-built energy calculations.
